subject: physics
title: Quantum & Nuclear Physics (HL) Adventure 2: Quantum uncertainty and atomic models
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet Schrödinger's wave equation and the uncertainty principle.
meta_desc: IBDP Physics HL — Schrödinger model, probability cloud, Heisenberg uncertainty, quantum tunnelling.
final_note: You learned Schrödinger replaced Bohr orbits with probability clouds; Heisenberg's ΔxΔp ≥ ℏ/2; quantum tunnelling allows e⁻ to cross barriers classically forbidden.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Bohr's orbits replaced by Schrödinger's wave function ψ.

|ψ|² = probability density of finding electron.

Orbital = region with high |ψ|² (e.g. s spherical, p dumbbell, d cloverleaf).

This is the modern atomic picture.

Δx · Δp ≥ ℏ/2

ℏ = h/(2π) ≈ 1.05 × 10⁻³⁴ J s.

You cannot know position AND momentum precisely. Tiny scales: matters; macroscopic: imperceptible.

Also: ΔE · Δt ≥ ℏ/2 (energy-time).

Particle has small but finite probability to penetrate a barrier even when classical KE < barrier height.

Used in:
- Scanning tunnelling microscope (STM, Binnig + Rohrer Nobel 1986).
- α decay (α tunnels out of nucleus).
- Flash memory (e⁻ tunnel into floating gate).
- Fusion in stars (protons tunnel through Coulomb barrier).
